notes: §1985:VII.4.6.4 GR7 is a prohibition laid on the program: "Within a USE procedure, there must not be the execution of any statement that would cause the execution of a USE procedure that had previously been invoked and had not yet returned control to the invoking routine." It states no result for a program that does so, and it leaves a USE procedure free to cause the execution of a different one. EmitUseMachinery gives each declarative its own slot of the per-program __useActive array and routes every selection through the one __RunUse invoker (EmitRunUseBody): a procedure that is not active runs, nested inside another when a statement of that other raised it, and its slot is cleared when it returns; a procedure selected while its slot is set is not re-invoked and the selecting statement falls through, so the forbidden execution does not recurse. At --std 85 the unit is free of the exception-condition model (>>TURN, RESUME and the exception-checking PERFORM are refused there, probed), so EmitUseMachinery picks the void form of the guard, which only declines; the EC-FLOW-USE raise of §2023:14.9.49.4 GR2 is the other arm and is never emitted there. The witness has file F1's procedure raise file F2's, and both run. Probed further at --std 85 on sequential files: F1's procedure fails a READ of F1 itself (46) and is not re-entered; it then raises F2's procedure, which fails a READ of F1 and is not handed F1's active procedure either; both complete, the run ends with exit 0, and F1's procedure runs again on the next error after it has returned.

next.reason: 1985: "there must not be the execution of any statement that would cause the execution of a USE procedure that had previously been invoked"; 2023: "if a statement raises an exception condition that would cause the execution of a USE procedure ... the EC-FLOW-USE exception condition is set to exist". 1985 forbids re-entering an active USE procedure and leaves the outcome undefined. 2023 instead defines the outcome: the EC-FLOW-USE exception condition is set to exist.
